text.p: A South Carolina man who raped and murdered two women after escaping from a prison work crew in 1984 was executed by lethal injection on Friday.

Frank Middleton Jr., 33, was pronounced dead at 1:22 a.m. EST (0622 GMT). He declined to make a final statement, but moments before the execution he lifted his head and tried to peer out the window at the official witnesses.
"What are you people looking at?" he asked. "I'm going into the promised land." Then, as the drugs flowed into his veins, he grunted, "Ha ha ha."
Nine hours earlier, he had eaten his last meal of fried chicken, french fries, corn on the cob and Coca-Cola.

After his last-minute court appeals failed, Middleton's supporters had tried to arrange a meeting for him with Gov. David Beasley so Middleton could prove he was a changed man. But Beasley denied a clemency request and said a personal meeting was not warranted.
A group of death penalty opponents held a candlelight vigil outside the governor's mansion on Thursday and later gathered outside the prison.
Middleton had spent 11 years on Death Row for killing Shirley Mae Mack of Charleston in June 1984. He had been sentenced to life in prison for killing Janell Garner two days earlier.

Middleton escaped from a minimum-security prison work crew in 1984 while serving a six-year sentence for stabbing a 13-year-old boy. He attacked 23-year-old Garner while she was on her way to buy milk for her baby, dragging her into a churchyard where he sexually assaulted, suffocated and repeatedly stabbed her.

Two days later, Middleton, who was then 22, raped and suffocated Shirley Mae Mack, a 49-year-old night-shift cook, while she was walking home from work. Later he returned to burn her body in a shallow grave.
Mack's husband, Bernard, witnessed the execution, staring at Middleton with clenched hands and a furrowed brow. He did not acknowledge reporters and declined to make a statement.
The state Supreme Court had overturned Middleton's 1985 murder convictions, saying he couldn't be tried for both murders simultaneously.

But after a second trial for Mack's murder in 1986, a jury convicted him again and he was sentenced to death. Middleton was convicted again in 1987 of murdering Garner, for which he was sentenced to life in prison.
